source: CogniLoad (2025) synthetic benchmark for CLT-style load in LLMs
finding: Benchmark gives each load its own dial: intrinsic difficulty d, distractor ratio rho (extraneous), task length N (called a proxy for germane). 22 reasoning LLMs tested. Length N is the dominant stressor.
numbers: 13 open models: 100 puzzles per config (~14,000 per model); Gemini-2.5, gpt-5 family, DS-R1: 10 per config. d in {1,3,5,7,10}; N in {20,50,100,250}. At N=250 only gpt-5 0.76 and o3 0.68 stay above 50%; most 0.20-0.30. DS-Llama-70B 0.89 to 0.66 from N=20 to 50.
quote: Our operationalization of N as a proxy for conditions demanding GCL, for example, is an abstraction.
limits: No scaffold ablation. Mapping germane load to task length is the authors' own admission of abstraction. Only deductive English puzzles.
agent_relevance: Load can be split by dials in machines, but 'germane = length' shows the three-way split is a design choice, not a measurement. Treat each dial as its own knob.

source: CogniLoad (2025) intrinsic difficulty results
finding: Intrinsic difficulty (element-interactivity analogue) hurts weak models far more than strong ones. By d=5, 12 of 22 models are below 50%.
numbers: o3 0.96 to 0.93 and gpt-5 1.00 to 0.97 from d=1 to d=3; small models drop 0.10-0.25. At d=10 gpt-5 0.82, o3 0.80, weakest about 0.10-0.15.
limits: Exact-match accuracy only; no human baseline.
agent_relevance: Load limits are model-relative, so step size in the schema should fit the weakest model used.

source: CogniLoad (2025) distractor ratio results
finding: Extraneous (distractor) load gives a U-shaped curve, not a straight line: worst accuracy at 25-50% needles, better at both extremes. Not a simple additive effect.
numbers: gpt-5 0.97 to 0.89 to 0.91; o3 0.93 to 0.89 to 0.88; gemini-2.5-flash-lite 0.38 to 0.53; Phi-4-reasoning-plus 0.59 to 0.45; EXAONE-Deep-32B 0.47 to 0.32.
limits: Text says rho 5-95; appendix shows seven levels (5,10,25,50,75,90,95).
agent_relevance: Supports De Jong's point that load types interact; more distractors is not always worse. Do not assume a linear cost of extra context.

source: Adapala (2025) Cognitive Load Limits in LLMs: Benchmarking Multi-Hop Reasoning (ICE benchmark)
finding: Interleaved Cognitive Evaluation varies extraneous tokens (20/50/80%) around multi-hop QA. Three of five models scored zero everywhere, so the load effect could be tested for only two.
numbers: 200 questions (50 SEC, 100 FanOutQA, 50 MINTQA). Control to Saturation 80%: Gemini-2.0-Flash 0.85 to 0.72; GPT-4o-0613 0.65 to 0.55. Llama-3-8B, Llama-3-70B, Mistral-7B: 0.00 in every cell. Gemini load slope beta=-0.003, p<0.001; GPT-4o beta=-0.002, p=0.07.
limits: Paper calls its results 'preliminary and circumscribed'. About 32% of GPT-4o outputs lacked a final answer (12% after post-processing). Temperature 0 makes '10 replications' unclear. Some references look like placeholders.
agent_relevance: A cautionary case: a CLT-flavoured LLM paper with weak evidence. Do not cite it for a robust extraneous-load effect.

source: Adapala (2025) ICE: length-matched control and residue
finding: Length-matched neutral filler did not explain the Gemini drop, so harm comes from distractor content, not length alone. Distractors placed before the task (residue) were not significantly worse.
numbers: Gemini Long Control vs Control p=0.45; Residue vs Control p=0.12. Hop recall: Gemini 0.90 control to 0.75 at 80% load; GPT-4o 0.80 to 0.65. Residue vs procedural similarity r=0.42 (Gemini, p<0.01), r=0.35 (GPT-4o, p<0.05).
limits: Residue effect not significant, so the 'attentional residue' reading is weak.
agent_relevance: Content of distractors matters; prune off-task material, not just tokens.

source: Zhang (2025) Cognitive Load-Aware Inference (CLAI)
finding: Zero-shot meta-prompt (CLAI-Prompt) rates intrinsic load, sets a token budget, filters context (extraneous), then reasons. A fine-tuned version (CLAI-Tune) is also reported. Claimed 35-45% fewer tokens at about equal accuracy.
numbers: Llama-3-70B GSM8K: CoT 92.5% at 485 tokens vs CLAI-Prompt 92.3% at 310 (36.1% less). MATH 53.9% at 812 vs 53.5% at 525. Llama-3-8B: GSM8K CoT 90.1/450 tokens, Prompt 89.8/290, Tune 91.5/255; MATH 50.2/49.9/52.1; HumanEval 73.2/72.5/74.8. LongBench QA F1: full context 65.2, LLMLingua 68.1, CLAI-Prompt 69.3 at 4.2x compression.
limits: Single author, no seeds or confidence intervals, round numbers; Llama-3-8B MATH 50.2% looks high versus commonly reported figures, so verify before relying. ICL/ECL/GCL are defined by prompt, not measured independently. No ablation separating the three loads.
agent_relevance: Plausible but unverified: budgeting tokens by rated difficulty. Our G1 (check-driven, not self-rated) conflicts with model-rated load; test it ourselves.

source: Zhang (2025) CLAI: how load types are operationalised
finding: ECL is 'wasteful computation', GCL is token budget given to productive reasoning, ICL is problem complexity from a model self-rating 1-10. The paper itself says low token count is not the goal.
numbers: Stage 1 budgets e.g. 50 tokens for easy, 500 for hard. Attention scores proposed as a proxy for productive tokens.
limits: Three terms are redefined in LLM terms with no independent measure, the same circularity De Jong flags for humans.
agent_relevance: Three-load words can be reassigned freely in LLM work, so 'CLT-based' on its own is weak evidence.

source: Shang et al. (2026) United Minds or Isolated Agents? CoThinker under CLT (TMLR)
finding: Multi-agent system built from CLT: split intrinsic load across specialist agents; shared memory and moderated routing for transactional load. Gains on reasoning-heavy tasks, losses on instruction-following where overhead (extraneous) dominates.
numbers: LiveBench, Gemini-1.5 Flash-8B/Flash/Pro; Holm-corrected paired bootstrap B=2000. Reasoning vs CoT +5.1 pp (p=0.001); Data Analysis vs IO +5.3 pp (p<.001); vs MAD up to +12.8 pp (p<.001). Instruction-following: vs IO -1.2 pp; three Holm-significant losses.
limits: Gains over DMAD often miss Holm significance. CLT supplies the story after the results; no ablation proves the load split is the reason. Uses perplexity as a load proxy.
agent_relevance: Boundary: extra structure helps when intrinsic load is high and hurts when low. Matches our guardrail against forced extra steps on easy items.

source: Shang et al. (2026) CoThinker cross-model and boundary check
finding: Authors state single-agent CoT suffices when intrinsic load is low; multi-agent helps when the task splits into distinct sub-problems. Cross-model checks used GPT-5-Nano, Qwen3-30B-A3B, Qwen3-32B, GPT-OSS-20B, Gemini-2.5-Flash, GPT-4.1-Mini.
numbers: Constrained setting (8192 tokens, greedy), LiveBench: Gemini-2.5 Math 76.3 vs IO 59.3, Reasoning 69.2 vs 31.0; GPT-4.1 Math 40.0 vs 34.0, Reasoning 70.8 vs 40.8.
limits: Partial results only; some row labels garbled in PDF text, so model-to-row mapping for the standard setting is not recorded.
agent_relevance: Gate extra structure by task difficulty rather than always on.

source: Wang et al. (2026) Beyond Accuracy: Cognitive Load Framework for Tool-use Agents (ToolLoad-Bench)
finding: Assumes load is additive: total = intrinsic + E x extraneous, with success = exp(-(k x load + b)). E is fitted per model. Accuracy shows cliffs as either load rises. Germane load is dropped.
numbers: 500 instances. Overall accuracy: xLAM2-32B 78.8%, GPT-4o 68.0%, Qwen3-32B 55.2%, Qwen3-8B 38.6%, Llama3.3-70B 17%. Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit used to claim calibration.
quote: the total cognitive load of a task is the sum of the cognitive loads of its constituent function call nodes
limits: Additivity is a postulate, not tested against an interaction term, so it cannot answer De Jong's circularity objection. Extraneous load is scored by an LLM judge.
agent_relevance: A modern machine paper assumes additivity and drops germane load; weak guide. If we measure load, fit an interaction term.

source: Gong, Wan, Wang (2024) Working Memory Capacity of ChatGPT: An Empirical Study (AAAI)
finding: Verbal and spatial n-back with ChatGPT shows decline with n and an apparent capacity near 3; noise lowers it, CoT raises spatial scores. Authors read it as a human-like limit.
numbers: d-prime drops to about 1 at n=3 in three of four verbal variants; 50 blocks of letters per condition; open models (Bloomz-7B, ChatGLM-6B, Vicuna-7B/13B) had very low capacity; GPT-4 not tested above n=3.
limits: Hu and Lewis (2025) show much of the drop is task misunderstanding. Capacity near 3 is not a fixed constant.
agent_relevance: Do not borrow a human WM number (3-4 chunks) for the agent; measured 'capacity' depends on the prompt.

source: Hu and Lewis (2025) Do Language Models Understand the Cognitive Tasks Given to Them? N-back (ACL Findings)
finding: Reanalysis of the Gong claim. Weak models make errors consistent with a different m-back task, so poor scores reflect task comprehension and task-set maintenance, not only a capacity limit.
numbers: Tiers by 2-/3-back retrieval accuracy: T1 >80% on both, T2 50% and 40%, T3 20%. Llama-3.1-70B retrieval accuracy at n=8,9,10: 75.25%, 66.08%, 57.1% (task accuracy 83.33%, 78.25%, 71.92%).
limits: Open models; GPT-3.5 not rerun the same way.
agent_relevance: A failure on a load-style task can be a comprehension problem; check the task is understood before blaming load.

source: Hu and Lewis (2025) in-context curriculum
finding: Prepending 1-back to n-back demonstrations (in-context curriculum) lifts large-n performance sharply, undermining a fixed-capacity reading.
numbers: Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct with curriculum at n=8,9,10: retrieval 79.83%, 80.17%, 71.67%; task accuracy 90.08%, 90.08%, 84.75% (versus 83.33%, 78.25%, 71.92% without).
limits: One strong model; effect on weaker tiers is smaller.
agent_relevance: Worked examples and graded practice raise machine 'capacity', the same direction as CLT's worked-example effect.

source: Hu and Lewis (2025) task-set drift and attention analysis
finding: Intermediate models start on the right task and drift toward a simpler m-back as errors accumulate. Strong models have attention heads that retrieve the n-back token; weak ones do not.
numbers: Qwen2-72B-Instruct top head 71.98% mean retrieval attention vs Qwen1.5-14B-Chat 38.95%; Qwen2-72B has 3.2x the count of high-MRAT heads. Retrieval log-probability peaks at m=n for the strong model.
limits: Correlational; head-level reading.
agent_relevance: Re-state the task at each step in a long loop; drift looks like load but is task-set loss.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context (GSM-IC)
finding: One irrelevant sentence added to grade-school math cuts accuracy sharply; fewer than 30% of base problems are solved consistently. Mitigations: exemplars with distractors, an instruction to ignore irrelevant info, self-consistency.
numbers: GSM-IC-4K; base-problem accuracy for text-davinci-003 80.0 (CoT), 81.0 (LtM). Self-consistency with 20 samples adds over 11 points micro accuracy (35.5 for 0-CoT); best macro accuracy still only 45%. Role-overlap distractors drive macro accuracy to 0 for text-davinci-003 on problems over 2 steps.
limits: 2022-era models.
agent_relevance: Direct extraneous-load test in a machine. Cheap fixes (say 'ignore irrelevant info', show a distractor example) fit our scaffold. Samples are not independent, so vote with a check (G4).

source: Shi et al. (2023) GSM-IC: which prompts are robust
finding: Least-to-Most prompting is the most robust to irrelevant context and stays flat across step count, while CoT and Program fall at four or more steps. Distractor exemplars do not hurt original GSM8K.
numbers: Instructed prompting improved CoT, LtM and Program in every Table 3 comparison. Correct answer is in the 20 samples for 99.7% of problems (CoT and LtM).
limits: Old models; benchmark now saturated.
agent_relevance: Decomposing into sub-questions (our operators) is also the more distraction-robust form.

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2025) GSM-Symbolic (ICLR)
finding: Adding one clause that looks relevant but does nothing (GSM-NoOp) causes large drops; models often convert it to an operation. More clauses lower accuracy and raise variance.
numbers: Drop on NoOp up to 65% (Phi-3-mini); as plotted, o1-preview -17.5, o1-mini -29.1, GPT-4o -32.0, GPT-4o-mini -40.0 points. 8 shots of the same question with correct reasoning did not fix it.
limits: 'No real reasoning' is the authors' hypothesis; figure values read from a plot.
agent_relevance: Machine analogue of intrinsic x extraneous interaction: harm grows with the task's own complexity. Pre-filter the problem statement before reasoning.

source: Levy, Jacoby, Goldberg (2024) Same Task, More Tokens (FlenQA)
finding: Padding input with irrelevant text lowers reasoning accuracy far below the context limit, wherever the key text sits; CoT does not reliably fix it.
numbers: Average accuracy falls from 0.92 to 0.68 by 3000 tokens across models; 300 samples per point (600 per figure). CoT helps GPT-4, Mixtral 8x7B, Mistral Medium, GPT-3.5 in most cases but lowers Gemini-Pro at long length.
limits: Synthetic padding; five models.
agent_relevance: Length alone costs accuracy; keep working context short and rebuild it per step.

source: Levy et al. (2024) FlenQA next-word metric
finding: Next-word prediction accuracy correlates negatively with reasoning accuracy, so length-robustness cannot be inferred from language-modelling scores.
numbers: Figure 6, 300 samples per point; correlation negative.
limits: Closed models limited to word-accuracy probes.
agent_relevance: Judge load by task accuracy, not by fluency or loss.

source: Liu et al. (2024) Lost in the Middle (TACL)
finding: Accuracy is U-shaped by position of the relevant document: best at start or end, worst in the middle, even in long-context models.
numbers: GPT-3.5-Turbo with 20 documents and the answer in the middle falls below its closed-book score of 56.1%.
limits: 2023 models; position effects differ in newer models.
agent_relevance: Put the active problem and constraints at the start or end of each prompt.

source: Liu et al. (2025) Mind Your Step (by Step): CoT can reduce performance where thinking hurts humans (ICML)
finding: Tasks where verbal deliberation hurts humans also see CoT hurt models in three of six archetypes. Extra reasoning is not always productive load.
numbers: Implicit statistical learning: o1-preview vs GPT-4o absolute drop 36.3%. Another task: GPT-4o -23.1%, Claude 3 Opus -8.0%, Gemini 1.5 Pro -6.05%, Llama 3.1 70B -8.8%; Claude 3.5 Sonnet -1.8% (p=0.969). Exception-learning: GPT-4o needed 331% more steps with CoT.
limits: Models and humans do not share all constraints; a heuristic only.
agent_relevance: Supports G1: do not force thinking on a schedule.

source: Xu et al. (2024) Cognitive Overload: Jailbreaking LLMs with Overloaded Logical Thinking
finding: Cognitive-overload prompts (multilingual, veiled expression, effect-to-cause reasoning) jailbreak all studied LLMs; CLT-inspired defenses (in-context demos as worked examples, defensive instructions) barely help.
numbers: Attack success rate rises with language distance from English for Vicuna, MPT, Guanaco and ChatGPT. Defense table shows high residual success rates (one ChatGPT cell 88.3%).
limits: Table layout in the PDF text is scrambled, so only trends are reliable.
agent_relevance: CLT is used as analogy for attack and defense; the worked-example defense did little. Do not rely on load-reduction tricks for safety.

source: Eliav (2026) The Cognitive Divergence (preprint)
finding: Non-peer-reviewed preprint states CLT has three 'additive' components and treats the LLM context window as working memory without a capacity ceiling.
numbers: Context windows 512 tokens (2017) to 2,000,000 (2026); human effective context span estimated 16,000 to 1,800 tokens by extrapolation.
limits: No peer review; extrapolated human data; repeats additivity without the critiques.
agent_relevance: Example of the additive three-load claim repeated uncritically; not evidence.

source: De Jong (2010) Cognitive load theory, educational research, and instructional design: some food for thought
finding: Background only, not opened this session. The human-side critique: additivity questioned, load types may affect each other circularly, measures unclear. The machine papers here either assume additivity (c10) or redefine terms per paper (c06, c07).
numbers: No numbers recorded this session.
limits: Not read by this agent; see other angle files for the primary reading.
agent_relevance: Reason to hedge any CLT-labelled claim in schema notes.

source: Synthesis across machine papers on the three-load split
finding: Across the papers read: intrinsic and extraneous dials can be separated in machines (c01, c03, c10), but germane is mapped to length (CogniLoad), token budget (CLAI), or dropped (ToolLoad). None test an interaction term or an independent load measure.
numbers: Of 4 papers that name the three loads, 3 define germane differently, 1 omits it, 0 test additivity.
limits: My own reading across sources, not a measured result.
agent_relevance: Schema should use concrete knobs (length, distractor share, step count, check results), not the words intrinsic/extraneous/germane.
